name: AR-03
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans about 13 points Republican and Womack has held the seat since 2011
Overwhelming money edge: Womack has $2.4 million on hand versus roughly $6,000 for Ryerse
Prediction markets price the Republican side near 95 percent to hold the seat
No polls or expert ratings show any sign of competitiveness
model.rationale: The district's strong Republican lean, Womack's incumbency and lopsided financial advantage, and markets pricing the Republican near 95 percent all point the same direction, with no polling or ratings evidence of a race. The fundamentals-based estimate of a mid-teens Republican margin fits every available signal.
model.watch: Any late outside spending against Womack or a surprise poll showing a single-digit race would be the first sign of movement, but nothing currently suggests either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Arkansas's third district has been solidly Republican, and Steve Womack has held the seat since 2011. The district's partisan lean sits about thirteen points to the right of the country, and the national environment this year favors Republicans. Womack has raised roughly $1.9 million and holds $2.4 million on hand, while Democrat Robb Ryerse has raised about $120,000 with under $6,000 remaining. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings track the race, but prediction markets give the Republican side about a 95 percent chance of holding the seat. With the incumbent renominated, a large financial edge, and no signs of Democratic investment in the district, the race rates as Safe Republican. Ryerse, a pastor who also ran in 2018, would need an abrupt shift in the environment or resources to make this competitive.
